core.statement: Use 9 as a logical control ring / indexing lattice above binary hardware, not as a replacement for the physical radix of conventional digital logic.

binary_path.byte_fact: A byte has 8 bit positions indexed 0..7 and 2^8 = 256 possible bit patterns.
binary_path.one_hot_8: If exactly one of the 8 bit positions is active, there are 8 selectable lanes.
binary_path.ninth_logical_state: A ninth logical slot requires either a 9-bit one-hot ring (stored in a wider integer) or an encoded value 0..8.

bit_walk.interpretation: The user's 'andar um bit para um lado e para o outro' maps to masks + shifts/rotates + optional modulo wrap.

buffer_partition.sync: Barrier/phase-boundary semantics are architectural; exact runtime binding remains TOKEN_VAZIO until source-bound.
buffer_partition.note: L1/L2/L3 caches and generic buffers are distinct hardware concepts. They may be modeled as separate logical strata, but buffer is not a fourth cache level by definition.

compute_routes.octa_core: Eight physical/logical CPU cores can be mapped to slots 0..7 when observed on a target, while slot 8 may be a control/sync state only by explicit design. Do not infer a physical ninth core.
compute_routes.memory: Expose the same 0..8 control/index vocabulary to RAM-side queues only where useful.
compute_routes.storage: Expose the same vocabulary to storage queues/chunks only where useful.
compute_routes.sync: Use explicit barriers, sequence numbers, epochs or atomic state transitions; 'sync' is not itself a numeric proof of MOD9.

crc.software: Support parameterized CRC widths/polynomials (for example 8/16/32/64) instead of assuming one width.
crc.hardware: Use hardware CRC/CRC32C instructions only when the target actually exposes them; hardware implementations are usually polynomial/width constrained.
crc.cross_check: HW and SW results are comparable only when width, polynomial, init, refin, refout and xorout are identical.
crc.evidence_rule: HW==SW under matched parameters is an implementation cross-check, not a scientific claim.

io_masks.concept: Pin/line selection is naturally represented by bit masks and shifts.
io_masks.db25_boundary: DB25 is a connector form factor used by multiple electrical/protocol standards. RS-232 DB25 signaling is not generic 5 V TTL GPIO; legacy parallel-port DB25 also has direction/current limits. Bind the actual electrical standard and use a proper driver/interface before switching loads.
io_masks.six_lines_example: To select six logical lines, use a six-bit mask (for example 0x3F) or six one-hot positions; actual pin mapping is platform-specific.

relations: 8 one-hot lanes indexed 0..7 -> optional ninth logical control slot
3 banks x 3 slots -> MOD9 control ring
memory/storage/CRC -> routes that may share the control vocabulary without becoming the same hardware block

routes_for_integration.RafGitTools: candidate location for reusable bit-mask/rotate/mod9 helper functions
routes_for_integration.RLL: candidate location only if a runtime scheduler or data path explicitly uses this control ring
routes_for_integration.Termux_ARM: candidate target for executable smoke tests of shifts/rotates/CRC HW-vs-SW

token_vazio: Exact historical files/repositories that already implement every part of this lattice have not yet been exhaustively inventoried.
Exact meaning of slot 8: sync, sentinel, parity, control, data, or multiplexed role.
Exact binding of 3x3 banks to L1/L2/L3/buffer; do not infer physical equivalence.
Exact DB25 electrical target/protocol/pinout in the user's example.
Whether MOD9 should be encoded as one-hot 9-bit, compact 4-bit digit, or both per subsystem.
antiregression: 8 bits != 8 total binary values; 8 bits have 256 patterns.
logical MOD9 != physical CPU core count.
